title: Grace Periods, Late Fees and Arrears Thresholds under Belrose Layaway and Hold Agreements
content:
# Arrears schedule

Credit control keeps one schedule of the figures that govern a late scheduled payment on each plan of Belrose Layaway and Hold Agreements: the grace allowed after a scheduled payment date, the fee for a late payment, the most late fees one agreement may carry over its whole term, and the days past due at which the agreement is marked delinquent and at which the merchandise is taken back.

| Plan | Grace period (calendar days after the scheduled payment date) | Late fee (USD) | Most late fees over the whole term | Days past due at which the agreement is marked delinquent | Days past due at which the merchandise is taken back and the agreement forfeits |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 30-Day Hold Agreement | 3 | 0.00 | 0 | 7 | 15 |
| 90-Day Layaway | 5 | 15.00 | 2 | 14 | 45 |
| 6-Month Layaway | 7 | 20.00 | 3 | 21 | 60 |
| 12-Month Bridal Layaway | 10 | 25.00 | 5 | 30 | 90 |
| Special Order Layaway | 5 | 20.00 | 3 | 14 | 45 |
| Gift Registry Layaway | 7 | 20.00 | 4 | 21 | 60 |

## Notes to the schedule

- The grace period is counted in calendar days after the scheduled payment date, during which the payment is still treated as on time.
- The 30-Day Hold Agreement carries a late fee of 0.00 and a ceiling of 0 late fees, which is to say it charges no late fee at all, however late a payment is; it still marks the agreement delinquent at 7 days past due and takes the merchandise back at 15.
- The ceiling on late fees is a count of fees over the whole term of the agreement, not a sum of money.
- The delinquency and forfeit thresholds are counts of calendar days past due.
